note:
We report a transiting planet candidate around TIC 458191673 (TYC 8605-1484-1), a V = 11.1 K dwarf at 65.5 pc, found in an independent search of TESS full-frame-image light curves of about 600 nearby K and M dwarfs that have never been observed at 2-minute cadence. Seven sectors from 2019 to 2026 show 62 transits with period P = 2.570687 ± 0.000005 d, depth 802 (+89/−80) ppm and duration 1.68 h (SNR 22), implying a planet radius of 2.22 ± 0.23 Earth radii.

The signal passes every test available to us. Odd and even transits agree and there is no significant secondary eclipse. The depth is consistent across sectors, and the stellar density implied by the transit shape matches the catalogue value. Difference imaging places the source on the target and disfavours all 221 Gaia neighbours within 90 arcsec. Gaia DR3 astrometry and radial velocities show no sign that the target is a binary. In a leave-one-season-out test, each of five seasons is predicted from the others and shows the dip at the predicted times. The identical search on upside-down light curves never produces a signal this strong. TRICERATOPS gives a false-positive probability FPP = 0.033 ± 0.004 and NFPP = 8e-5. All eclipsing-binary scenarios together have <0.1% probability, and the residual FPP comes from a planet transiting an unresolved companion star.
